solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, enumeration length); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; the grid proves the blog's answer wrong at 16 down, corrected here

entries.clue: Comrade after revolution has little time for US politician (8)

indicators.note: a revolution turns the letters of COMRADE over into a new order

blocks.note: COMRADE rearranged
T is the abbreviation for time

annotation.surface: An old party comrade, after a political revolution, barely has a moment for an American politician.
annotation.walkthrough: The Cold War flavour of 'Comrade' and 'revolution' points away from American politics, yet the letters of the comrade become the Democrat.
annotation.definitionFit: A Democrat is a member of one of the two main US political parties.

entries.clue: Process till has cryptic set (6)

indicators.note: something cryptic is puzzling and obscure, so SET is scrambled

blocks.note: to till soil is to dig it
SET rearranged

annotation.surface: A cash register comes with a coded setting that someone has to work through.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Till' reads as a cash register, but here it is the farming verb, to turn the soil.
annotation.definitionFit: To digest information is to process it mentally, as the stomach processes food.

entries.clue: Immature but sweet little thing? Pack your bags, hubby! (9)

blocks.note: a husband is 'my man'
the order to pack your bags is 'get out'

annotation.surface: A wife dismisses her childish husband, sweet as he may be, telling him to pack and leave.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition sounds like a description of the husband, but it is a vegetable: a mangetout is a pea picked while the pod is young and sweet enough to eat whole. The wordplay is the wife's line, 'Man, get out!'
annotation.definitionFit: Mangetout peas are harvested immature, small and sweet, pod and all.

entries.clue: Vehicle over pit in purplish-red (7)

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
a pit is a coal mine

annotation.surface: A vehicle crashes into a pit and ends up covered in something reddish.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above, so the vehicle sits on top of the pit.
annotation.definitionFit: Carmine is a deep crimson or purplish-red colour, originally from cochineal.

entries.clue: Northbound sailor after a book of charts (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, travelling north means reading from the bottom up
the sailor comes after A in the answer

blocks.note: taken as printed
an old salt is a sailor; it is written upwards as TLAS

annotation.surface: A sailor heading north needs a set of charts to find the way.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old salt' is a common crossword sailor alongside AB and TAR.
annotation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound collection of maps or charts.

entries.clue: Starter of ravioli in set meal (6)

indicators.note: a starter comes first, so take the first letter of ravioli
'in' means placed within, so R is put inside the other word

blocks.note: a set or group is a bunch; R goes inside it after the first letter
first letter of ravioli

annotation.surface: A plate of ravioli is served as the opening course of a set menu.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Starter' and 'set meal' dress the clue as a restaurant menu, but 'set' is the noun bunch and the meal is the one between breakfast and lunch.
annotation.definitionFit: Brunch is a meal eaten late in the morning.

entries.clue: Questionable article for reading (7)

indicators.note: something questionable is not straight, so the letters of ARTICLE are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: A dubious newspaper piece is offered as reading material.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a shoddy article worth reading; the reading is a performance, as at a poetry recital.
annotation.definitionFit: A recital is a public reading or recitation of a text.

entries.clue: Commotion inside casino is excessive (5)

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of casino, through 'is', into the start of excessive

annotation.surface: Someone complains that the racket inside a casino is too much.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the word breaks: casi-NO IS E-xcessive.
annotation.definitionFit: Noise and commotion both mean a loud disturbance.

entries.clue: Religious nursing home for the love of God! (8)

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold, so HOLY holds NEST

blocks.note: holy = religious; this word does the nursing, cradling the home
a nest is a home

annotation.surface: An exasperated cry about a care home run by a religious order.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nursing home' is one phrase in the surface but splits in the wordplay: 'nursing' is the container, 'home' the contents.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Honestly!' and 'for the love of God!' are both exclamations of exasperation.

entries.clue: Weak dons knowing a little (8)

indicators.note: to don is to put on, so LIGHT wears SLY around it

blocks.note: a weak drink is light
a knowing look is a sly one; this is the garment the weak word puts on

annotation.surface: Feeble university lecturers know only a little.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dons' looks like Oxford lecturers, but it is the verb: LIGHT puts on SLY like a coat, giving S(LIGHT)LY.
annotation.definitionFit: Slightly means to a small degree, a little.

entries.clue: All energetic, one dancing in event where seats available? (7,8)

indicators.note: dancing letters move about into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

annotation.surface: Everyone lively takes to the floor at a function where there are chairs free.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Seats available' sounds like a theatre or a party, but the seats are parliamentary ones, up for election.
annotation.definitionFit: In a general election every seat in parliament is contested, so all are available.

entries.clue: Organism that is equipped with eyewear? (7)

definitions.note: a species is a kind of organism rather than a single one

indicators.note: SPECS is fitted out with IE inside it

blocks.note: specs are spectacles; they are fitted out with IE before the last letter
i.e. = id est, 'that is'

annotation.surface: A creature that wears glasses.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the silly picture of a bespectacled organism; 'equipped with' reads as wearing the glasses but tells the eyewear to take the letters in.
annotation.definitionFit: A species is a kind of organism, loosely used for the organism itself.

entries.clue: Wimpy, but wy? (7)

blocks.note: read as a limp complaint about someone feeble, and meant as the definition: cowardly
read as a misspelt 'but why?', and meant as a description: the word WHY with its middle letter, its gut, taken out

annotation.surface: A timid question so feeble it cannot even spell itself.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wy' is not a misprint: it is WHY with its insides removed, and a word with no guts is gutless, which is what wimpy means.
annotation.definitionFit: Gutless means lacking courage, which is what wimpy means.

entries.clue: Divine woodland inhabited by heartless cobra (8)

indicators.note: FOREST has CA living inside it
COBRA loses its middle, leaving the outer C and A

blocks.note: forest = woodland; the snake's remains live inside it
C-obr-A with the middle removed

annotation.surface: A heavenly wood that happens to be home to a cruel snake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Divine' reads as an adjective, heavenly, but it is the verb: to divine the future. FOREST holds CA: FORE(CA)ST.
annotation.definitionFit: To divine is to predict or foresee, which is to forecast.

entries.clue: Fishy cod eaten in story (8)

indicators.note: something fishy is suspect and not straight, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A suspicious tale about somebody eating cod.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fishy' goes so naturally with 'cod' that it hides its job as the anagram indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short story about a real incident.

entries.clue: Boozer all squiffy, offensive customer initially arrested (5)

indicators.note: squiffy means tipsy, so the letters of ALL stagger into LAL
take the first letters of offensive and customer
LAL holds OC, as the police hold a suspect

blocks.note: ALL rearranged; this does the arresting, holding the two initials
first letters of offensive and customer

annotation.surface: At a pub where everyone is tipsy, a rude punter gets taken away by the police.
annotation.walkthrough: A boozer is British slang for a pub, and the local is the pub nearest home. Scrambled ALL holds OC: L(OC)AL.
annotation.definitionFit: Your local is the pub you regularly drink in; a boozer is a pub.

entries.clue: Real choir performing in Belgian city (9)

indicators.note: the letters act out a new arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A proper choir gives a concert in a city in Belgium.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface places the choir in the city; the city itself is made from the choir's letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain factual definition: the answer is a large former coal-mining city in Wallonia, southern Belgium.

entries.clue: Given dessert, perhaps, spoilt (5-3)

blocks.note: dessert is eaten with a spoon, so being given it is being fed with one
a spoilt child has had everything handed to them, never having to feed themselves

annotation.surface: A child pampered with puddings.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'perhaps' admits that dessert is only one example of spoon food; in Britain the dessert course is often called 'pudding' and eaten with a spoon.
annotation.definitionFit: Spoon-fed means fed with a spoon, and figuratively over-indulged.

entries.clue: Assemble a palindrome? (3,2)

blocks.note: to erect a tent or shelf, raising it into place
a word that reads the same in both directions, as the answer written without its space does

annotation.walkthrough: The second half describes the answer's own spelling: PUTUP is the same backwards, and 'put up' is also the setter's usual signal to reverse a down entry, which a palindrome survives unchanged.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to erect a tent or flat-pack shelf is to assemble it.

entries.clue: Space he created for fruit (7)

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: A man clears some room to keep fruit.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder crosses the word break: SPACE plus HE.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the answer is a stone fruit in the plural, and 'fruit' serves as a collective noun for them.

entries.clue: As mummy, for example, smeared paint on back of daddy (8)

indicators.note: paint smeared about has its letters spread into a new order
the back of a word is its last letter
'on' means placed next to, so the scrambled paint is attached to the letter from daddy

blocks.note: e.g. = for example
last letter of daddy
PAINT rearranged

annotation.surface: A child daubs paint on dad's back while mum looks on.
annotation.walkthrough: The family picture of mummy and daddy hides the embalmed kind of mummy; 'As mummy' means of the kind a mummy is.
annotation.definitionFit: The classic mummy is Egyptian, preserved in ancient Egypt.

entries.clue: Lean around queue, observing launch of ball (5-2)

indicators.note: 'around' means surrounding, so the first word wraps round the second

blocks.note: lean = thin, as in lean meat; it goes round the queue
a queue is a row of people

annotation.surface: A spectator leans round the queue to watch the ball being put in play.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lean' looks like a verb in the surface but is the adjective, as in lean meat; a throw-in is how football restarts after the ball goes out over the touchline.
annotation.definitionFit: A throw-in restarts play in football by throwing the ball back onto the pitch.

entries.clue: Somewhat praiseworthy, phenomenal joiner? (6)

indicators.note: only some of the letters are used, a stretch from inside the phrase

blocks.note: the last two letters of praiseworthy run on into the first four of phenomenal

annotation.surface: Praise for a remarkable carpenter or other joiner.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain a joiner is a woodworker, which the surface suggests; the answer is the punctuation mark that joins words.
annotation.definitionFit: A hyphen joins two words or parts of words.

entries.clue: Garden where rod designed to catch fish (7)

indicators.note: ROD is redesigned into ORD
ORD catches CHAR inside it

blocks.note: ROD rearranged; it catches the fish in its middle
the char is a fish related to trout

annotation.surface: A garden where a fishing rod has been set up to land a catch.
annotation.walkthrough: The char is a crossword favourite among fish, alongside ide and ray. Scrambled ROD holds CHAR: OR(CHAR)D.
annotation.definitionFit: An orchard is a garden or enclosure of fruit trees.

entries.clue: Cut right through grotto (5)

indicators.note: R runs through the middle of CAVE

blocks.note: a grotto is a cave; R goes through its middle
R = right

annotation.surface: Someone cuts straight through a grotto.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut right' reads as one phrase, but 'right' belongs to the wordplay. CAVE with R through it gives CA(R)VE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to carve meat or stone is to cut it into shape.

entries.clue: Instant recovery in decent manner (7)

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, British slang for an instant
a rally is a recovery, as in prices or health

annotation.surface: A sudden comeback made with good grace.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Instant' looks like an adjective describing the recovery, but it is a noun: 'half a mo' is British for a moment.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: acting ethically, in line with what is right, is acting decently.

entries.clue: Hundred in American numbers game (5)

indicators.note: 'in' means placed within, so the hundred sits inside the American numbers

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
Americans say math where Britons say maths; the hundred goes inside it

annotation.surface: A hundred appears in a US numbers game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Numbers game' reads as one phrase, but 'numbers' is the school subject and 'game' the definition. MATH holds C: MAT(C)H.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a football match or a tennis match is a game.

entries.clue: I’m offering my counsel anyway, at a fair price? (3,4,3,5)

blocks.note: the phrase that prefaces unsolicited advice
read literally: sold for exactly its value

annotation.surface: An adviser offers an opinion, whether or not it is wanted, as if selling it cheaply.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading of the idiom as a price.
annotation.definitionFit: The idiom introduces advice the speaker admits may not be valued; taken literally it names a fair price.

entries.clue: Smart squirrels marginally inside their home? (6)

indicators.note: only the margins, the first and last letters, of squirrels are used
'inside' means within, so the squirrels' edges sit within their home

blocks.note: outer letters of squirrels
a drey is a squirrel's nest; the two edge letters go inside it

annotation.surface: Clever squirrels are only just tucked inside their nest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Their home' refers back to squirrels, so it is the squirrel's nest, the drey. DREY holds SS: DRE(SS)Y.
annotation.definitionFit: Dressy means smart, elegantly dressed.

entries.clue: Again travelling around capital in Harare, an African (8)

indicators.note: the letters travel about into a new order
the capital, first, letter in Harare

blocks.note: anagram fodder
first letter of Harare
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: An African is on the move again, travelling around the Zimbabwean capital.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Capital in Harare' tempts you to think of Harare itself, the capital of Zimbabwe, but it gives only the capital letter H.
annotation.definitionFit: A Ghanaian is a person from Ghana, in West Africa.
